currentContext.business: The Company manufactures a wide-ranging portfolio of premium crucibles and foundry-related accessories used for melting, holding, treatment and casting of both ferrous and non-ferrous metals and alloys, primarily silicon carbide and clay graphite crucibles. Its products serve customers in automotive, aerospace, jewelry, mining, industrial machinery, electrical equipment and railways, and are distributed across Asia, Europe, Africa, the Middle East and North America. During the year the Company's promoters sold their 75% stake to Foseco India Limited, bringing it into the Vesuvius Group, a global leader in molten metal flow engineering with operations across 40 countries.

Foundry solutions: Foundry-related accessories and consumables for melting, holding, treatment and casting of ferrous and non-ferrous metals

currentContext.strengths: Backing of the global Vesuvius Group following the FY26 acquisition by Foseco India Limited - access to Group technology, expertise and an international network spanning 6 continents, 40 countries, 75 sales offices, 6 R&D centers and 54 production sites|Close to four decades of crucible engineering experience refining silicon carbide and clay graphite formulations|Long-standing relationships with established Indian industrial groups including Tata Group, Hindustan Pencils, Indian Railways, Jindal Saw, Titan Company Limited, Sundaram Clayton Group, Mahindra CIE and Bajaj Auto|ISO 9001:2015 certified quality management system supporting consistent, precision-engineered product delivery|Deep materials-science and application-engineering know-how enabling customer-specific, precision-built solutions
currentContext.strategies: Aligning processes, systems and procedures with Foseco India Limited / Vesuvius Group following the change in promoter control, to support a smooth transition and operational integration.|Strengthen its position as a preferred supplier in the non-ferrous metals industry through product quality, technical expertise and customer-centric solutions.|Continue focusing on innovation, operational excellence and value-added services to support the next generation of products and manufacturing processes.|Leverage growth opportunities in the domestic market while closely monitoring developments in international markets and supply chains.|Maintain a 'zero-harm' workplace safety culture and world-class safety system as an ongoing operating priority.|The Company follows a voluntarily-adopted Dividend Distribution Policy (per SEBI LODR Regulation 43A) that sets out a transparent framework balancing shareholder returns with retaining sufficient capital for future growth, covering when dividends may or may not be expected, the financial/internal/external parameters considered, and how retained earnings are to be utilised. For FY2025-26 the Board recommended a final dividend aligned with this policy.
currentContext.expansion: No new plant, line or capacity-expansion project with a commissioning/completion timeline is disclosed in this bundle. The only physical capacity addition noted is a 1 MW rooftop solar power plant, installed at the facility in three phases, which contributed 33% of total electricity consumed at the site during FY2025-26; the facility also has a rainwater storage capacity of 500 m3 for surface-water catchment. Separately, a capital-commitments note discloses two figures for contracts remaining to be executed on capital account, but the routed block carries only one dated period header for two value lines, so the figures cannot be reliably attributed to FY26 vs the FY25 comparative and are therefore not usable as a dated disclosure (see capex_disclosed).
currentContext.mdna: Indian market expected to remain a key growth driver, supported by continued expansion in manufacturing activity, infrastructure development and favourable domestic demand trends.|Indian foundry industry - the Company's largest end-market segment - continues to demonstrate resilience and steady growth, aided by increasing localisation, government manufacturing initiatives and demand from automotive, engineering, railways and construction.|Sustained strength in precious metals prices and increasing activity in the precious metals refining sector expected to support the Company's global business performance.|Continued investments in infrastructure and industrial development across India anticipated to create additional growth opportunities in the Company's core operating segments.|Export markets outlook remains cautious near-term due to geopolitical tensions (evolving US-Iran conflict), trade protection measures, supply chain disruptions, elevated freight and energy costs, and volatility around the Strait of Hormuz.|Precious metals refining segment expected to remain comparatively resilient versus other export-oriented segments despite global uncertainty.|Indian foundry industry growth prospects supported by infrastructure development, increasing localisation, Government initiatives ('Make in India', production-linked incentive schemes), and demand from electric vehicles, renewable energy, railways and industrial machinery.|Industry headwinds include volatility in raw material and energy costs, environmental compliance requirements, global supply chain disruptions, pricing pressures and availability of skilled manpower.

risks.note: 75% of the Company's shares were acquired by Foseco India Limited (Vesuvius Group) via SPA dated August 22, 2025, completed November 12, 2025; the Company is still in the process of aligning its processes, systems and procedures with the new parent, creating integration risk.

The outlook for export markets is flagged as cautious near-term due to ongoing geopolitical tensions (including the evolving US-Iran conflict), trade protection measures, supply chain disruptions, and elevated freight and energy costs; volatility around the Strait of Hormuz could further impact global manufacturing activity and input costs.

risks.risk: Raw material and energy cost volatility
risks.note: The Indian foundry industry, the Company's largest end-market, continues to face volatility in raw material and energy costs, which pressures input costs and margins.
Supply chain disruptions are cited as an ongoing industry-wide challenge affecting both domestic operations and export-oriented business.
Environmental compliance requirements are flagged as a continuing challenge for the Indian foundry industry in which the Company operates.
The industry continues to face challenges around availability of skilled manpower, a structural constraint on operations and growth.

risks.risk: End-market and price concentration in precious metals refining
risks.note: The Company's global business performance is linked to sustained strength in precious metals prices and activity in the precious metals refining sector; a reversal in precious metals prices or refining activity would be a headwind.
